messages.subject: Workshop on R statistical package breedR
messages.subject_clean: Workshop on R statistical package breedR
messages.body_plain:
Dear Colleagues,

In the frame of the Trees4Future project  (http://www.trees4future.eu/), we are inviting for a workshop concerning  the use of the statistical package breedR. The workshop will be held at the Forest Research Institute, Sekocin Stary, Poland (10-11 December 2015).

The package breedR provides frequentist and Bayesian statistical tools to build predictive models useful for breeders, quantitative genetists and forest genetic resources analysts communities. It aims to assess the genetic value of individuals under a number of situations, including spatial autocorrelation, genetic/environment interaction and competition.

Workshop will be led by Leopoldo Schanchez and Facundo Muñoz from INRA (Orléans) with the help of local organizers.

Participants are obliged to cover their costs of travel, meals and accommodation. There is no other fee to attend in the workshop.

The registration is possible until 4 December.

More details

messages.subject: Heritability and other news
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I’m glad to (finally!) announce the incorporation in the latest version of breedR (0.10-19) of one of the most requested features <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/issues/16>: the automatic (under certain circumstances) computation and reporting of the heritability.

Furthermore, I added a vignette <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/Getting-started#breedr-guides> on computing heritability. It covers all possible scenarios, and the available options (Delta method, simulation from asymptotic distributions, and bootstrapping).

Comments and contributions are welcome, as always.

Other news <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/blob/master/NEWS> include another vignette on handling missing values, a direct interface to PROGSF90 options (giving more control on the REML process), and a new mechanism for installing breedR which brings several advantages (more on that later).

Best wishes
ƒacu.-
​

messages.subject: installing breedR
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

in the latest version of breedR the installation process had several
changes (for the better)

 1.

    Before, breedR shipped 32bit versions of PROGSF90 for the three
    Platforms.
    Now, I created an online repository in the breedR site
    <http://famuvie.github.io/breedR/> from where the appropriate
    binaries for your platform *and* architecture are downloaded
    automatically at install time.
    From the user’s perspective, the only thing that has changed is that
    now you will benefit from 64bit programs if your architecture
    supports it. Also, I don’t waste your hard disk by storing binaries
    suited to other platforms.

 2.

    Now you can |install.packages('breedR')| (or use RGui/RStudio/*
    menus) just like with any other package.
    Moreover, breedR will be updated automatically when you
    |update.packages().|
    This also avoids using |devtools| for installation, which is a heavy
    package to have for such a simple task.
    The only requirement is to configure breedR’s repository in your
    system. See instructions in the website
    <http://famuvie.github.io/breedR/>.

Best wishes
ƒacu.-

​
--
